newsitem.title: FRANCE: Youth, consumers need Internet safeguards - France.
newsitem.headline: Youth, consumers need Internet safeguards - France.

text.p: France said on Wednesday it welcomed an appeal by U.S. President Bill Clinton for a laissez-faire policy on Internet commerce but said young people and consumers should be protected.
"We agree with the United States that we must avoid holding back (Internet) development by imposing a paralysing regulatory scheme," Junior Minister for Industry Christian Pierret said.

"But we must not ignore the serious difficulties that nations are encountering in attempting to assure the protection of consumers and to safeguard fundamental ethical principles, particularly with regard to young people," Pierret said in a statement.
Clinton said in Washington on Tuesday that he wanted the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to begin work on establishing a free-trade zone for internet commerce within the year.

U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky later said she hoped to start with a basic group of countries -- including the EU -- to secure agreement on a hands-off policy on internet commerce and build global support from there.

Pierret said France wanted to be an active participant in the formulation of European and international policy on Internet and would make its views known at a coming meeting in Bonn on global information networks.

He said Paris hoped the European Union would adopt a common position on the technology, saying the Internet would "without doubt be one of the most important elements of economic growth and job creation."
